newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga resumes output at Vigdis oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Saga resumes output at Vigdis oilfield.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday it had restarted output at the 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) North Sea Vigdis oilfield after finding a temporary solution to problems with the gas compressor system.
Saga spokesman Bjoern Schibevaag said Vigdis resumed production on Friday after a four-day stoppage and was now producing between 25,000 and 30,000 bpd.
"We have not solved the problem with the gas compressor system at Vigdis yet," he said.
"We have found a temporary solution by moving the gas from the production into the Snorre gas system through a crossover. It means we don't have to flare the gas from Vigdis."
Due to Norwegian regulations governing gas flaring, the compressor must be functioning before production can go ahead.
Schibevaag said the company was working on a new gas seal that it hoped to have in place and tested before August 25.
Vigdis is scheduled to go into maintenance on August 25 to coincide with a turnaround planned on the Gullfaks A platform.
Vigdis, which came on stream in January, five months ahead of schedule, has had a series of production stoppages since April linked to a design fault in the gas compressor system.
